tasks.short: Plan meetings with colleagues, discuss teaching and research issues, share and comment on documents, write up agreements, and follow up actions.

steps.what: Education lecturer plans meetings with colleagues by e-mail
Education lecturer collaborates with colleagues to address teaching and research issues in meetings
Education lecturer shares documents as e-mail attachments and merges colleagues' comments
Education lecturer writes up agreements and actions
Education lecturer follows up actions with colleagues by e-mail

tasks.design: Meetings are planned with a calendar poll ({CALENDAR}). Documents sit in a shared folder where colleagues comment in the same file ({DOCS}), so versions are not mailed and merged. Agreements are typed into a shared notes template during the meeting, and actions sit on a shared task list ({PROJECT}) that sends reminders, so the lecturer does not chase by e-mail. Discussing issues stays with the lecturer and colleagues.
tasks.previous_blocker: Dates, versions and actions went back and forth by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared documents, calendar polls and task lists are standard at universities.
tasks.still_hard: Colleagues at other universities use other tools.
tasks.human_edge: Turning a disagreement about teaching into a shared plan.

evidence.claim: Shared documents with comments, calendar polls and shared task lists are standard collaboration tools.

assumptions: Boundary: from the issue raised to actions followed up; research itself is outside.
Input contract: colleagues use the shared folder; fallback is e-mail.
Colleagues update tasks in about the time replying to e-mails took.
research_questions: Are agreed actions completed more often?

incremental.description: Education lecturer sets up shared folders and task lists.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly colleagues outside the university; high: a team that works in shared files.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect course evaluations and pass rates, map learning outcomes across courses, discuss revisions with colleagues, decide changes, and revise course materials and descriptions.

steps.what: Education lecturer evaluates courses by collecting evaluations, pass rates and accreditation feedback
Education lecturer maps learning outcomes across courses in a spreadsheet
Education lecturer discusses revisions with colleagues and the curriculum committee
Education lecturer plans curricula, course content and methods of instruction
Education lecturer revises course materials and course descriptions

tasks.design: A course dashboard ({BI}) combines evaluation scores and pass rates per course, so they are not collected by hand. Each course's learning outcomes are tagged to the programme outcomes in the course catalogue ({OTHER}), which generates the curriculum map instead of a spreadsheet. Course description forms open with last year's text and track changes, so only changed parts are rewritten. Discussing and deciding revisions stay with the lecturer and colleagues.
tasks.previous_blocker: Results were gathered by hand and curriculum maps kept in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Course catalogues tag outcomes; dashboards combine course results.
tasks.still_hard: Outcomes are tagged unevenly by different lecturers.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which part of the programme leaves new teachers unprepared.

evidence.claim: Course catalogues can tag course outcomes to programme outcomes and generate a curriculum map.
Course analyses use aggregated student results; personal data need a lawful basis.

assumptions: Boundary: from the review due to materials revised; programme accreditation is outside.
Input contract: outcomes tagged in the catalogue; fallback is spreadsheets.
Revision decisions stay with the lecturer and committee.
research_questions: Do gaps in the curriculum show up earlier?

incremental.description: Education lecturer tags outcomes for new courses.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a programme with few tagged courses; high: a programme with all outcomes tagged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Hold office hours with students, schedule appointments by e-mail, answer repeated questions by e-mail, and note agreed follow-up.

steps.what: Education lecturer maintains regularly scheduled office hours to advise and assist students
Education lecturer schedules appointments with students by e-mail
Education lecturer answers repeated course questions by e-mail
Education lecturer notes advice and agreed follow-up

tasks.design: Students book office hour slots themselves in the lecturer's booking page ({CALENDAR}), so appointments are not set by e-mail. A course question page in the learning system ({LMS}) answers the questions that come every term, such as placement deadlines and portfolio rules, so the lecturer answers fewer repeated e-mails. Advising students stays with the lecturer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Appointments and repeated questions were handled one e-mail at a time.
tasks.enabler_now: Booking pages and course question pages are standard tools.
tasks.still_hard: Students still e-mail questions the page answers.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a student teacher is struggling in their placement school.

reach.learn: Whether slots are easy to book.

evidence.claim: Booking pages let students pick free slots in a calendar.
Notes on students are personal data and need a lawful basis.

assumptions: Boundary: from the student request to follow-up noted; study advice by advisers is outside.
Input contract: booking page linked to the lecturer's calendar; fallback is e-mail.
Students book in about the time an e-mail took.
research_questions: Do more students use office hours?

incremental.description: Education lecturer updates the course question page.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small group with few requests; high: a large cohort with many e-mails.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the student's study progress, look up programme rules and options, advise on curricula and careers, write the advice note, and refer students to other services.

steps.what: Education lecturer reads the student's study progress and results before the meeting
Education lecturer looks up programme rules, minors and placement options
Education lecturer advises students on academic and vocational curricula and on career issues
Education lecturer writes the advice note in the student file
Education lecturer refers students to career services or student counsellors by e-mail

tasks.design: A study progress view in the student information system ({OTHER}) shows credits, results and remaining requirements by fixed rules, so the lecturer does not piece them together before each meeting. Programme rules, minors and placement options sit on one catalogue page. The advice note uses a short template with fields in the student file, and referrals go through a form that routes to career services or counsellors with the student's consent, instead of an e-mail. Advising stays with the lecturer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Progress was pieced together from several screens and referrals sent by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Student information systems show progress against programme rules.
tasks.still_hard: Students with exemptions or transfers do not fit the standard rules.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a student decide whether teaching is really for them.

evidence.claim: Student information systems can show credits and remaining requirements against programme rules.
The AI Act's high-risk education points cover admission, assignment and evaluating learning outcomes; advice here is given by a person.

assumptions: Boundary: from the advice meeting to the student referred; formal study advice decisions are outside.
Input contract: programme rules set up in the student information system; fallback is searching screens.

incremental.description: Education lecturer checks progress for students with exemptions.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many students with exemptions; high: standard full-time students.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The education lecturer keeps discussing teaching with colleagues, deciding revisions and advising students; e-mail scheduling, merged versions, hand-gathered results and pieced-together progress shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A lecturer with more time with student teachers.
